_comment: One-time announcements delivered to the AI on session start, at most once per project.
Use these when a release changes behavior or adds a setting the user should know about —
something a changelog would cover but nobody reads. The AI surfaces the message, acts on it,
then acknowledges it so it never fires again for that project.
notice_key           stable id, never reuse or rename (the acknowledgement is keyed on it)
message              exactly what the AI should tell or ask the user
action_required      true = AI must prompt and wait; false = inform only
applies_from_version fires only once applies_to_db has reached this version
introduced_in        package version that added it (informational)
Leave applies_to_db and applies_from_version null to fire for every project regardless of
schema version. Set both to tie a notice to the migration that introduced the change.

notices.title: Scheduled backups are now on by default (every 7 days)
notices.message:
AIMFP now checks on session start whether it has been more than backup_interval_days since the last backup, and asks before creating one. The default is every 7 days.

This is new because the pre-existing check only fired after 30 days of INACTIVITY — meaning an actively developed project was never backed up, which is backwards from what backups are for.

ASK THE USER NOW: does a 7-day backup cadence suit this project, or would they prefer a different interval or none at all? Then apply their answer with update_user_setting('backup_interval_days', '<days>') — use '0' to turn scheduled backups off entirely. If they have no preference, leave it at 7 and say so.

Backups capture .aimfp-project/ state (tracking databases and the blueprint), not source code — git covers that. Only backup_count archives are kept, oldest rotated out.

notices.title: Tasks now remember the files worked on for them
notices.message:
This project's database was upgraded to schema 1.12, which adds task-to-file links.

Until now get_task_context and get_task_files returned no files for any task (they looked files up through flows, via a column that never existed). Now, whenever you reserve, finalize, catalog, or update a file — or finalize, catalog, or update its functions or types — while a task, subtask, or sidequest is in_progress, that file is linked to it automatically.

Existing tasks have no links yet. TELL THE USER this briefly, and for any task currently in_progress, link the files already worked on with link_files_to_task(task_id, file_ids, task_type) so its context is complete. Completed tasks can stay unlinked.

notices.title: Themes, flows and modules are now enforced and reported
notices.message:
AIMFP now enforces its modularity layer: themes (stable project areas) group flows (the behaviour the code implements), flows group files, and modules group reusable code. Completion paths now link the themes they advance, and milestones link the flows they build.

What changed for the AI:
- reserve_file / reserve_files REQUIRE flow_ids: a list of flows, or an explicit null for a config/data file (optionally with no_flow_reason).
- add_flow REQUIRES theme_ids: every flow belongs to at least one theme.
- aimfp_status / aimfp_run now include structure_summary (the themes -> flows map) and structure_health (gaps), aimfp_end reports gaps, and the watchdog raises structure_* reminders until gaps are fixed.
- New batch tools: add_flow_themes, add_path_themes, add_milestone_flows, move_files_to_flow, move_flows_to_theme (and note-required remove_* counterparts); get_structure_health lists everything.

TELL THE USER how many gaps data.structure_health reports for this project (total_gaps and the biggest categories). Existing projects usually have many: themes were never linked to flows, and paths/milestones had no links at all before this release.

ASK THE USER NOW: should we backfill the modularity layer this session (link every flow to a theme, every open path to its themes, every open milestone to its flows, give unflowed files a flow or a no_flow_reason, split oversized flows), or later? Apply the answer; if later, record add_note(note_type='deferred') so it is not lost.
